summary: James Adam (1860–1907) worked in philosophy and other fields. He studied at the University of Aberdeen around 1876–1880 and Gonville and Caius College around 1880–1884.

James Alan Matisoff is a scholar in linguistics, sinology, and tibetology. He studied at Harvard, International Christian University, and UC Berkeley (PhD 1967). He taught at Columbia (1966–1969) and served as professor emeritus of linguistics at UC Berkeley (1970–2002).

James Atkinson (1780–1852) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology after studying at the University of Edinburgh. He served at the India Government Mint in Kolkata (1812, 1818) and was Assistant Persian Professor at Fort William College in 1818.

James B. Apple works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin–Madison in 1996, studying under John D. Dunne and Geshe Lhundub Sopa, among many other academic and traditional teachers.

James Blumenthal (1967–2014) studied Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, completing his PhD at the University of Wisconsin–Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa. He taught at Oregon State University (attested 2004, 2013–2015) and Maitripa College (attested 2013–2015).

James Burgess (1832–1916) worked in Indology and archaeology. Educated at Glasgow and Edinburgh, he served as Secretary of the Bombay Geographical Society (1868–1873), Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1886–1889), and Vice President of the Royal Society of Edinburgh (1908–1914).

James Burnell Robinson works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Richard Hugh Robinson and Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and he held a post as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Northern Iowa (attested 1996).

James C. Dobbins is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Yale University by 1984 and served as Fairchild Professor of Religion and East Asian Studies at Oberlin College (attested 2015–2019).

James Charles Colebrooke Sutherland (1792–1844) was an Indology scholar who studied at the East India Company College and under Thomas Roebuck at Fort William College. He served as professor of law at Presidency University.

James Darmesteter (1849–1894) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied under Michel Bréal at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1872–1877), where he held a post (~1877–1894) alongside a professorship at the Collège de France (1885–1894).

James Duerlinger works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin–Madison (~1964–1968) under Sheldon Pollock and joined the faculty at the University of Iowa in 1971.
James Dwight Dana (1813–1895) studied at Yale College from around 1830 to 1833 and held a post at Yale University from around 1850 to 1892.
James Fergusson (1808–1886) studied at the Royal High School, Edinburgh, and was a member of the Royal Asiatic Society in 1840.

James Fieser is a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at Berea College and Purdue University (~1982–1986), and held posts at the University of Tennessee and the University of Tennessee at Martin around 1992.

James G. Mullens works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Simon Fraser, the University of Victoria, and McMaster University (PhD 1994) under Graeme MacQueen, and held a post at the University of Saskatchewan in 1989.
James Gibbs (1825–1886) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1870–1879) and President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1870–1881).

James H. Austin is an academic neurologist and scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Nanrei Sohaku Kobori and other Zen teachers. His academic posts include the University of Oregon (~1956–1965) and the University of Colorado (~1965–1992).

James Hadley (1821–1872) worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Yale College and under Edward Elbridge Salisbury, tutored at Middlebury College (1845), and served as Professor of Greek at Yale University from 1845 to 1872.

James Haughton Woods (1864–1935) was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar. He studied at Harvard, Strasbourg, and under Charles Rockwell Lanman, Paul Deussen, and Arthur Venis, becoming a professor at Harvard University in 1914.

James Irving Manatt (1845–1915) worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Grinnell and Yale under William Dwight Whitney, and held posts at Denison (~1874–1876), Marietta (~1877–1884), Nebraska–Lincoln (~1884–1889), and Brown University (~1892–1915).
